newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NO PROBLEMS FOR RANGERS IN SCOTTISH CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NO PROBLEMS FOR RANGERS IN SCOTTISH CUP.

text.p: Cup holders Rangers breezed into the fourth round of the Scottish F.A. Cup with a comfortable 2-0 win over first division leaders St Johnstone at Ibrox on Saturday with first-half goals from Erik Bo Andersen and Sebastian Rozental.
The Dane continued his recent good scoring streak with the opener after 10 minutes, while the Chilean Rozental struck his first goal on his home debut 20 minutes later.
Unlike in England, there were no major upsets with all the premier division clubs overcoming opponents from lower divisions.

Hearts, beaten by Rangers in last season's final, raced into a three-goal lead inside 22 minutes against third division Cowdenbeath before winning 5-0 thanks to goals from Colin Cameron (8th), David Weir (12th), John Robertson (22nd pen and 63rd) and Neil Pointon.
Premier division Dunfermline were also too strong for third division Ross County, winning 4-0 at home with Andy Smith scoring twice, and Harry Curran and Hamish French adding the others.

Motherwell, who are involved in a struggle against relegation, went through to the fourth round after winning 2-0 at first division Partick Thistle, while Dundee United also beat first division opposition by the same score, winning 2-0 at Stirling Albion.
Celtic, looking to add to their record of 30 Cup final wins since their first in 1892, play first division Clydebank on Sunday.
